Return to footnote * Referrer
There is no reason indicated because the employer was found non-compliant for an incident that occurred before new regulations came into effect on December 1, 2015.

## Reasons employers may be found non-compliant
Employers may be found non-compliant for one or more of the following reasons:
- The employer couldn’t show that the information they listed in the offer of employment was true, for a period of 6 years, starting on the first day the foreign national worked for them. Provision: 209.2(1)(b)(i)
- The employer didn’t keep documents that showed they met the conditions of employing a foreign national, for a period of 6 years, starting on the first day the foreign national worked for them. Provision: 209.2(1)(b)(ii) or 209.3(1)(c)(ii)
- The employer didn't have the money to pay the wages agreed to with a live-in caregiver. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(iii)(C)
- The employer couldn’t show that the description they gave for the job on the Labour Market Impact Assessment application was true, for a period of 6 years, starting on the first day the foreign national worked for them. Provision: 209.3(1)(c)(i)
- The employer didn't show up for a meeting with the inspector, to answer questions and give documents the inspector asked for. Provision: 209.4(1)(a)
- The employer didn't give the inspector the documents they asked for. Provision: 209.4(1)(b)
- The employer didn't show up for an inspection, and didn't help or give information to the inspector when asked to. Provision: 209.4(1)(c)
- The employer broke federal, provincial or territorial laws for hiring and recruiting employees in the province or territory where the foreign national worked. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(ii) or 209.3(1)(a)(ii)
- The pay or working conditions didn't match, or were not better than, what was listed on the offer of employment, or the job was not the same as what was listed on the offer of employment. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(iii) or 209.3(1)(a)(iv)
- The live-in caregiver wasn't living in a private home in Canada or was not providing unsupervised care for a child, senior or disabled person within the home. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(iii)(A)
- The hiring of the foreign national didn’t create new jobs or job stability for Canadian citizens or permanent residents. Provision: 209.3(1)(b)(i)
- The hiring of the foreign national didn’t result in Canadian citizens or permanent residents getting new or improved skills and knowledge. Provision: 209.3(1)(b)(ii)
- The employer didn't hire or train Canadian citizens or permanent residents as they agreed to. Provision: 209.3(1)(b)(iii)
- The employer didn't put in enough effort to hire or train Canadian citizens or permanent residents, as they agreed to. Provision: 209.3(1)(b)(iv)
- The employer was not actively engaged in the business that the foreign national was hired to work for (aside from live-in caregivers). Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(i) or 209.3(1)(a)(i)
- The live-in caregiver didn't receive private and furnished living space in the home. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(iii)(B)
- The employer didn't put in enough effort to make sure the workplace was free of any of the following: Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(iv) or 209.3(1)(a)(v)
- physical abuse
- sexual abuse
- psychological abuse
- financial abuse
- reprisal
- The employer stopped the foreign national from complying with an order or regulation made under the Emergencies Act or the Quarantine Act. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(v) and 209.3(1)(a)(vii)
- The employer stopped the foreign national from complying with a provincial law that governs public health. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(vi) or 209.3(1)(a)(viii)
- The employer didn’t provide wages to the foreign national that were substantially the same as those set out in the offer of employment, during the period the foreign national was required to isolate or quarantine themselves on entry into Canada. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(vii) and 209.3(1)(a)(xii)
- The employer didn’t provide the foreign national with accommodations that were separate from those provided to persons not in quarantine, and that permitted the foreign worker to remain at least 2 metres away from any other person. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(ix)
- The employer didn’t provide the foreign national with cleaning products for the purposes of cleaning and disinfecting the accommodations regularly. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(x)
- The employer didn’t provide a foreign national, who developed any signs or symptoms of COVID-19, with accommodations that had a bedroom and a bathroom solely for the use of the foreign national while they isolated themselves. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(xi)
- The employer didn’t provide adequate accommodations to a foreign national employed to perform work under an international agreement concerning seasonal agricultural workers between Canada and one or more countries. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(vi)
- The employer didn’t provide the foreign national with information on their rights in Canada, in their chosen official language, on or before their first day of work. Provision: 209.2(1)(a.1) or 209.3(1)(a.1)
- The employer didn’t make the information on the foreign national’s rights in Canada available in both official languages. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(ii.1) or 209.3(1)(a)(ii.1)
- The employer didn’t put enough effort into providing access to health care services when the foreign national was injured or became ill at the workplace. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(viii) or 209.3(1)(a)(xiv)
- The employer charged the foreign national fees related to their hiring, not including application processing fees. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(ix) or 209.3(1)(a)(xv)
- The employer didn’t make sure that the foreign national wasn’t charged fees by anyone involved in their hiring or recruitment process, not including application processing fees. Provision: 209.2(1)(a)(x) or 209.3(1)(a)(xvi)
- The employer didn’t obtain, and pay for, private health insurance that covers emergency medical care when the foreign national was not covered by provincial health insurance. Provision: 209.3(1)(a)(xiii)
Note: The information above is a summary only. Complete descriptions of the ways an employer can be found non-compliant are available in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations .

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: About the process
text:
## Extend or change the conditions on your work permit

## Fees
From $155

## Processing time
We couldn’t load the data. Try again
You must apply to extend or change the conditions on your work permit if
- it will expire soon, or
- you want to change employers or other conditions listed on it

## Apply at least 30 days before your current work permit expires
You should apply at least 30 calendar days before the expiry date of your current work permit.
To avoid delays, you should consider the processing time for in-Canada work permit applications . This increases the chance that we’ll process your application before, or shortly after, your current permit expires.

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: After you extend
text:
## After you extend

## If you applied online to extend or change your work permit
After you apply online, we’ll send you a letter in your account (WP-EXT except PGWP) that you can use as proof that you’re authorized to keep working, if you’re eligible .
- You can print this letter or show it with your current work permit.
- The letter is proof that you’re authorized to keep working under the same conditions as your original work permit until we process your application.
- You can keep working past the expiry date on the letter until we process your application if the conditions are the same as on your original work permit.

## Some applicants won’t receive a proof of authorized work letter
You’re not eligible to receive a letter (WP-EXT except PGWP) that proves you’re authorized to work if you
- applied for an extension to your work permit after your work permit expired
- applied for your first work permit in Canada

## Why there’s an expiry date on the letter
Your letter automatically lists an expiry date that’s 365 days from the date we receive your application. The expiry date will help satisfy concerns from your employer and health insurance providers about your status and authorization to work in Canada.

## If we don’t finalize your application by the date on your letter
If we don’t finalize your application by the date on your letter, you can still keep working until we make a decision .
If your employer or others need proof that you can continue to work, you can show them this web page.
Learn more about working while we process your application .

## If you applied without an LMIA or CAQ
If you don’t submit your labour market impact assessment (LMIA) or Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) within 90 days of the date you submit your extension application, your application may be refused for being incomplete.

## How to submit your LMIA or CAQ
When you get your LMIA or CAQ, you must submit your missing document using the IRCC web form .

## If you applied on paper to extend or change your work permit
If you applied on paper, you won’t get a letter (WP-EXT except PGWP) that proves you’re authorized to work. This is because we need to make sure that your application is complete and that you meet the requirements to work.
If you applied to extend or change your work permit before it expired, you’re authorized to continue working under the same conditions as your current work permit .
You can show your employer proof that you submitted your application. Valid forms of proof include
- a copy of your work permit application
- proof that you paid your fees
- a copy of postal or courier tracking information

## Temporary resident permit applicants do not benefit from maintained status
Temporary resident permit (TRP) applicants can’t maintain temporary resident status while their application is being processed . This applies to both
- initial TRP applications, and
- any other TRP applications

## What happens if we approve your application
You’ll get
- an extension of your current work permit, or
- a work permit with new conditions on it, including
- the type of work you can do
- the employer you can work for
- where you can work

## Working while you wait for your work permit to arrive
We’ll send you a note in your online account letting you know your work permit has been approved. You can start working as soon as you receive this note.
You don’t have to wait until you get your work permit in the mail to start working.

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: If you can’t apply online
text:
## If you can’t apply online
Most people have to apply online to extend their stay in Canada as a worker. In a few cases, you may not be able to apply online .

## Apply on paper to extend or change the conditions on your work permit
Follow the steps below to apply on paper to extend your stay as a worker.

## Step 1: Get the application package
This package includes the application guide and all the forms you need to fill out.
Read the guide before you fill out the application form:
- Instruction Guide [IMM 5553]

## International Experience Canada applicants
If you’re extending your participation or changing your work permit under International Experience Canada (IEC), you must follow the IEC-specific instructions .
If your application is not completed properly, it may take longer for us to process it.

## Tips for downloading and completing the forms
- You can fill it out and save it using a computer.
- You’ll need Adobe Reader 10 or higher.
- You must also turn JavaScript on.
- Filling out the form on a computer is easier than filling it out by hand.
- Having trouble downloading the form? See, “ How do I download and open a PDF form? ”

## Documents
- Document Checklist [IMM 5556] (opens in a new tab)
- Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710]
- Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union [IMM 5409] (opens in a new tab)
- Use of a Representative [IMM 5476] (opens in a new tab)
If you have questions about the forms, find answers to your questions in the Help Centre .

## Step 2: Prepare your application package
Make sure you submit all the pages of the form.
- Click the “Validate” button at the top or bottom of the form.
- This makes sure that you answered all the questions in the form and will help you avoid processing delays.
- A new page with barcodes and a signature line will automatically be added at the end of your form.
- Print, sign and date the form.
- Print on white, bond-quality, non-glossy paper.
- Use a laser printer.
- Place the barcode page at the top of your package. If you have more than one package, place a separate barcode page on each one.
Find out more about the barcode form .

## Step 3: Pay your application fees
In most cases, your fees will include processing fees for you and anyone you include on your application.
Our instruction guide can help you understand which fees apply to you and show you how to pay them.

## Step 4: Submit your application
Submit your completed application to the address given in the application package. Make sure you include the fee receipt and all the necessary documents.

## Alternate formats
If you can’t apply online or use the forms above because of a disability, you can ask for other formats including large print and braille. Contact the Client Support Centre (in Canada only) or submit a Web form for other formats.

## Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker
You can’t fill out and save the application form using your Internet browser. To use the form, you need to:
- Use your computer (Mac or PC). The form won’t open on mobile devices (iPads, tablets, mobile phones, etc.)
- Install Adobe Reader 10 (or higher)
- Download the PDF file to your computer . Save the file in a place you can remember.
- Make sure you use Adobe Reader to open the form. Sometimes if you try to open the form directly, it will use your Internet browser to try to open it.
Note: If you are applying online , you don’t need to print and sign the form.

## Get the form
- Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710] (opens in a new tab)

## Having issues with the form?
- I can’t open my visa application form in PDF format. What can I do?
- After clicking the “validate” button on my visa application form, nothing happens and I don’t see the barcodes. Why is this happening?

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: How to apply
text:
## How to extend

## On this page
- Maintain your status
- Before you extend or change the conditions of your work permit
- How to extend or change the conditions of your work permit

## Maintain your status
If you apply to extend or change the conditions of your work permit before it expires, you’re legally allowed to stay in Canada while we process your application.
If your work permit expires while we process your application, find out if you can keep working .

## Temporary resident permit applicants do not benefit from maintained status
Temporary resident permit (TRP) applicants can’t maintain temporary resident status while their application is being processed . This applies to both
- initial TRP applications, and
- any other TRP applications

## Date and time we receive your application
To maintain your status , we must receive your application before your work permit expires. We determine the date and time an application is received 2 ways:
- If you apply online: You must submit your application before midnight Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) on the day your work permit expires.
- Our online application system uses UTC.
- Make sure you know the difference between your local time and UTC.
- If you apply on paper: We stamp paper applications the day we receive them at the case processing centre.
- If we receive an application after your work permit expires, we’ll count back 7 days and use that as the date received.

## Before you extend or change the conditions of your work permit
Before you apply, make sure your employer has completed all the required steps .

## Labour market impact assessment–required work permits
Some jobs require a labour market impact assessment (LMIA). Your employer is responsible for submitting the application for an LMIA. In most cases, you should wait to apply for a work permit extension until your employer gives you a positive LMIA decision letter.
Check the processing times for LMIA applications.

## If you don’t have your positive LMIA or CAQ decision letter
You may be able to submit your work permit extension application while your employer’s application for an LMIA or Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) is being processed.
You must meet the following criteria if you want to extend your work permit before you receive your positive LMIA or CAQ decision letter:
- Your work permit expires in two weeks or less.
- Your employer submitted a complete application for an LMIA or CAQ.
- You submit all required documents within 90 days of when you submit your application.
If you don’t submit your LMIA or CAQ within 90 days, your application may be refused for being incomplete.

## What to include when you apply for your work permit extension
If you don’t have your new LMIA or CAQ, you must include additional documents when you submit your application.

## Check the expiry date on your passport
You can’t extend your work permit beyond the expiry date of your passport . Make sure your passport won’t expire before the requested end date of your permit.

## How to extend or change the conditions of your work permit
In most cases, you must apply online to extend or change the conditions of your work permit.

## How applying to extend your work permit online helps you
- You can make sure your application is complete before you submit it.
- Unless you’re a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) holder, you’ll get a work permit extension letter (WP-EXT) that proves you can keep working under the same conditions as your current work permit .
- You won’t get this letter if you apply on paper, because we won’t know if your application is complete until we review it.
- There are no courier fees or mail delivery time—we get your application instantly.
- You can quickly submit more documents online (if we ask you to).
- You get updates on the status of your application directly in your online account.
- As of June 21, 2024, you can no longer apply for a PGWP at a port of entry (airport, land or marine border) when entering Canada.

## Compare your work permit expiration date with our processing time
To avoid delays, you should consider the processing time for in-Canada work permit applications . This can help you decide when to apply and increases the chance that we’ll process your application before, or shortly after, your current permit expires.
Processing time: We couldn’t load the data. Try again
Send your work permit extension application once you have all your documents ready.

## Renew your provincial or territorial and federal identity documents before your current work permit expires
If you applied to extend your work permit and then your permit expires, you have
- maintained your status , and
- authorization to work without a permit until we make a decision on your application
You can keep working under the same conditions of your current work permit. If you have an employer-specific work permit, this means having the same
- employer
- job
- work location
Open work permit holders can still change employers and jobs.

## Renewing provincial or territorial documents
While you’re on maintained status , you won’t be able to renew documents issued by your province or territory, such as your
- driver’s licence
- health card
Make sure your documents are valid before your work permit expires.

## Applying for or updating the expiry of your social insurance number (SIN) card
While on maintained status (while your work permit is expired), you can’t apply for a SIN card or update the expiry date of your current SIN. You can, however, keep working under the same conditions as those on your initial work permit.
Find out what you need and how to apply for or renew your SIN card .

## Step 1: Make sure you have what you need
Sign in or create an IRCC secure account to start your application.
Sign in to start your application
To apply online, you’ll need
- a scanner or camera to create electronic copies of your documents
- a valid credit or debit card

## If you can’t apply online
You can submit a paper application if either
- you can’t apply online because of a disability
- there’s a problem with the online application
- In some cases, you may be able to apply online if you follow special instructions.
What to do if you have problems applying online

## Step 2: Upload forms and documents
After you answer the questionnaire in your IRCC secure account, you’ll get a personalized document checklist.
You need to complete the following application form:
- Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker (IMM 5710)

## If you’re a Venezuelan passport holder with an expired passport (the printed expiry date has passed)

## If your Venezuelan passport was issued before June 7, 2019

## If your passport has been expired for less than 5 years
Your passport is considered valid for an additional 5 years after the printed expiry date (to a maximum validity of 10 years).
When you apply for temporary residence:
- Add 5 years to the printed expiry date shown on your passport, and enter it in the “Expiry date” field of the application form.
- Include a letter of explanation with your application stating: “I am a Venezuelan national with a Venezuelan passport, which has been extended for 5 years past the printed expiry date.”

## If your passport has been expired for 5 years or more
Your passport is only considered valid for an additional 5 years after the printed expiry date (to a maximum validity of 10 years).
If it’s been more than 5 years since the printed expiry date, your passport is considered expired. It is not valid to apply for temporary residence.
If you have an exceptional situation and can’t get a new passport or other acceptable travel document, you may still apply.
- Include a letter of explanation with details of your exceptional situation and why you can’t get a valid travel document.
- An officer will review your application and determine if you’re eligible even without a valid passport or travel document.

## If your Venezuelan passport was issued on or after June 7, 2019
If your passport is expired, it can’t be used to apply for temporary residence. You need to get a new passport or another acceptable travel document to apply.
Even if you apply online, you should read the instruction guide before you complete your application. The guide will explain how to complete each field on the form.

## If you apply without an LMIA or CAQ
If you're eligible to apply without an LMIA or CAQ , follow these instructions when you complete your application:
- Type the code CPTS2026 in the Job Title field of the IMM 5710 form.
- Include proof that you have a valid job offer.
- Provide either of the following documents depending on how your employer applied:
- a copy of the LMIA receipt confirmation number online applications
- a copy of the application sent to Service Canada or the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration paper applications
- Indicate all of the following in the Details of intended work in Canada section of your work permit application:
- the date the LMIA or CAQ request was sent
- the office it was sent to
- the employer’s name
- the confirmation number for the submission, if available

## Credit cards and prepaid cards
We accept credit cards and prepaid cards from:
- Visa ®
- MasterCard ®
- American Express ®
- JCB ®
- UnionPay ® (for online applications only; debit cards not accepted)
If you use a prepaid credit card, keep it for at least 18 months after you pay to make refunds easier. Find more on prepaid cards .
We also accept all Visa Debit cards.
The card you use doesn't have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application.

## Debit cards
It must:
- be from a Canadian bank using INTERAC ® Online , and
- be registered for online banking through your bank’s website.
We also accept all Debit MasterCard ® and Visa ® Debit cards. If your card has the Visa Debit logo on it, alone or with the INTERAC ® Online logo, select Visa Debit as your payment method.
The card you use does not have to be in your name. The cardholder’s name will appear on the receipt but it does not need to match your application.

## Letter that proves you’re authorized to work (WP-EXT except PGWP)
After you apply online, we’ll send you a letter (in your online account) that you can use as proof that you’re authorized to keep working.
You can print it and attach it to your current work permit, or show it to your employer. It’s proof that you’re authorized to keep working under the same conditions as your original work permit until we process your application.

## Priority processing for work permit applicants
We’re prioritizing certain work permit applications.

## Provincial nominees in certain specialized health care occupations
You may be eligible for faster processing for an employer-specific work permit if you
- have a full-time and non-seasonal job offer in one of the three eligible NOCs
- NOC 31100 – Specialist in clinical laboratory medicine
- NOC 31101 – Specialists in surgery
- NOC 31102 – General practitioners and family physicians
- have a support letter from a Canadian province or territory
- The letter nominates you as a permanent residence applicant through the Provincial Nominee Program.
- meet the general eligibility requirements (opens in a new tab) to apply for a work permit, depending on where you apply from
Get faster processing

## Other eligible occupations that perform or support essential services
We’re prioritizing the applications of people who perform or support essential services .
When you fill out the work permit application form
To get priority processing, follow these steps:
- Get the National Occupational Classification (NOC) number your employer entered on the
- offer of employment or
- labour market impact assessment (LMIA)
- Enter that number in the Job title box.
- This is box 4 in the Details of intended work in Canada section.
- You must enter only the number .

## NOC 2021
On November 16, 2022, we switched to the 2021 version of the NOC system.
If you apply for a work permit on or after November 16, 2022, make sure you use the NOC 2021 codes .

## Agriculture and agri-food occupations
NOC 2021 codes
- Butchers – retail and wholesale (NOC 63201)
- Meat cutters and fishmongers – retail and wholesale (NOC 65202)
- Agricultural service contractors and farm supervisors (NOC 82030)
- Livestock labourers (NOC 85100)
- Specialized livestock workers and farm machinery operators (NOC 84120)
- Harvesting labourers (NOC 85101)
- Nursery and greenhouse labourers (NOC 85103)
- Fish and seafood plant workers (NOC 94142)
- Labourers in food and beverage processing (NOC 95106)
- Labourers in fish and seafood processing (NOC 95107)
- Industrial butchers and meat cutters, poultry preparers and related workers (NOC 94141)

## Health-care occupations
NOC 2021 codes
- Nursing coordinators and supervisors (NOC 31300)
- Registered nurses and registered psychiatric nurses (NOC 31301)
- Specialists in clinical and laboratory medicine (NOC 31100)
- Specialists in surgery (NOC 31101)
- Police investigators and other investigative occupations (NOC 41310)
- General practitioners and family physicians (NOC 31102)
- Nurse practitioners (NOC 31302)
- Physician assistants, midwives and allied health professionals (NOC 31303)
- Respiratory therapists, clinical perfusionists and cardiopulmonary technologists (NOC 32103)
- Other professional occupations in health diagnosing and treating (NOC 31209)
- Pharmacists (NOC 31120)
- Medical laboratory technologists (NOC 32120)
- Medical laboratory assistants and related technical occupations (NOC 33101)
- Medical radiation technologists (NOC 32121)
- Cardiology technologists and electrophysiological diagnostic technologists (NOC 32123)
- Licensed practical nurses (NOC 32101)
- Paramedical occupations (NOC 32102)
- Nurse aides, orderlies and patient service associates (NOC 33102)
- Home child care providers (LMIA-required in-Canada applicants) (NOC 44100)
- Home support workers, caregivers and related occupations (LMIA-required in-Canada applicants) (NOC 44101)
You may be eligible for even faster processing if you
- have a full-time and non-seasonal job offer in one of the three eligible NOCs
- NOC 31100 – Specialist in clinical laboratory medicine
- NOC 31101 – Specialists in surgery
- NOC 31102 – General practitioners and family physicians
- have a support letter from a Canadian province or territory
- The letter nominates you as a permanent residence applicant through the Provincial Nominee Program.
- meet the general eligibility requirements to apply for a work permit, depending on where you apply from
Get faster processing

## Step 3: Pay the fees
We’ll ask you to pay your fees at the end of your application.
In most cases, your fees will include processing fees for you and anyone you include on your application.
Some applicants may be exempt from paying some or all work permit application fees.

Check if you need to give biometrics

## Step 4: Submit a complete application
Make sure you submit a complete application in your IRCC secure account. Your application may be refused if you’re missing documents or other required information.

## If you need to leave Canada and plan to return
If you applied to renew your work permit before it expired, you can leave Canada and come back, but there are some things you need to know .

## Step 5: Give your biometrics again after you apply If applicable
Even if you already have valid biometrics, you may want to give them again.
You might want to give your biometrics again before they expire if
- your biometrics will expire soon
- We can’t issue you a work permit that’s valid for longer than your biometrics.
- you applied for permanent residence and your application was refused
- you only gave partial biometrics with your application (fingerprints or photo)
To give your biometrics
- Pay the biometrics fee when you apply.
- Wait for your biometrics instruction letter and then book your biometrics collection appointment as soon as you can to avoid processing delays.
Give your biometrics

## Problem with the online application
If you’re trying to apply for a work permit online in one of the categories below, you may have problems getting the right result. If you’re not sure if this applies to you, ask your employer.

## LMIA-exempt applicants
- Permanent residence applicants in Canada who
- used Express Entry to submit their permanent residence application, and
- have received an acknowledgment of receipt letter (A75)
- Open work permit pilot program for permanent residence applicants in the spouse or common-law partner in Canada class (A70)
- Foreign physicians coming to work in Quebec (C10)
- Refugee claimants (S61)
- Failed refugee claimants waiting for removal who need to support themselves (S62)
- Persons under an unenforceable removal order (S62)
- Live-in caregivers who have submitted their permanent residence application (A71)
- In-Canada applicants under the Home Child-Care Provider Pilot or the Home Support Worker Pilot (C90) and their family members (C91)
- Post-graduation work permit extension (C43)
- Destitute students (H81)
- Holders of a temporary resident permit that’s valid for a minimum of 6 months (H82)
- Start-up visa workers (A75)
- International Experience Canada: Extend your participation or change conditions on your work permit (C21)

## LMIA-required applicants
- Seafood-processing workers
- Agricultural workers who are not part of the Seasonal Agricultural Worker Program

## Visitors to Canada
- Visitors in Canada applying for an initial study permit, work permit or both who are accompanying a spouse holding a low-skilled work permit

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: Changing jobs or employers
text:
## Changing jobs or employers
If you have an employer-specific work permit and you want to change jobs or employers in Canada, you must apply for a new work permit , if you’re eligible.
You may be able to start your new job or work for a new employer before your work permit application is approved. You can request authorization to work while we process your application.
Open work permit holders can change employers at any time while their work permit is valid.

## Who’s eligible
To be eligible, you must meet the following conditions:
- You applied for a new employer-specific work permit in Canada .
- You currently
- have an employer-specific work permit , or
- are a worker who can work without a work permit ( not including business visitors or short-term workers under the Global Skills Strategy )

## If you lose your job
If you have lost the job connected to your employer-specific work permit and would like to continue working in Canada, you must
- get a new job offer and apply to change the conditions of your work permit
- stay in Canada
- stop working for this or any other employer until your new work permit is approved or we send you a work authorization email
Learn more about what to do if you lose your job .

## How to request authorization to work while we process your application
International Experience Canada (IEC) participants must first check that they can change employers with an IEC work permit .
To change jobs or employers, follow these steps after you apply for your new employer-specific work permit :

## Step 1: Let us know you want to change jobs or employers
Use the IRCC web form to let us know you need to change jobs or employers.
- Select See details under the Other category and then Continue to form , when prompted.
Under the Your enquiry section of the IRCC web form , copy the text below that applies to your situation. Make sure you fill out the sections in square brackets, which include the
- dates
- name(s) of employer(s)
- title of your job
If you applied on paper and don’t know your application number, include your courier tracking number. This will allow us to find your application.
If you have other questions, you need to fill out an IRCC web form .

## Avoid delays
You must include the code PPCHANGEWORK2020 when you copy and paste the text below. We can’t prioritize your request without this code.

## Message that work permit holders changing jobs or employers need to paste into the web form:
Priority Code PPCHANGEWORK2020: I am requesting consideration under the Temporary public policy to exempt foreign nationals in Canada from certain requirements when changing employment and ask that the applicable exemptions be granted until a decision is made on my work permit application or it is withdrawn.
I attest that I hold/held a work permit valid until [DATE] for employer [ name ] / in occupation [NOC code ] and I have received a new job offer for [new employer name ] / [new occupation NOC code ].
I have submitted my application for a work permit online or I submitted my paper application and the postal/courier tracking number is [ number ].
I intend to work for the [new employer name ] / [new occupation NOC code ] as specified in the aforementioned work permit.
I understand that providing false, misleading or incorrect information is a violation of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and may result in enforcement measures against me.

## Message that workers who have been exempt from holding a work permit need to paste into the web form:
Priority Code PPCHANGEWORK2020: I am requesting consideration under the Temporary public policy to exempt foreign nationals in Canada from certain requirements when changing employment , and ask that the applicable exemptions be granted until the decision is made on my work permit application or it is withdrawn.
I attest that I am/was authorized to work without a work permit for employer [ name ] / in occupation [NOC code ] until [DATE] and I have received a new job offer for [new employer name ] / [new occupation NOC code ].
I have submitted my application for a work permit online or I submitted my paper application and the postal/courier tracking number is [ number ].
I intend to work for the [new employer name ] / [new occupation NOC code ] as specified in the aforementioned work permit.
I understand that providing false, misleading or incorrect information is a violation of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and may result in enforcement measures against me.

## Step 2: Wait for our email authorizing you to work while we process your application
After you submit the web form, wait for us to email you.
We should respond in about 10 to 15 days. If you applied on paper, it will take longer to get the email.
The email will let you know if you’re authorized to work while we process your application. This email is not your work permit.
Check the processing time for work permit applications processed inside Canada.

## Problem with the online application
If you’re trying to apply for a work permit online in one of the categories below, you may have problems getting the right result. If you’re not sure if this applies to you, ask your employer.

## LMIA-exempt applicants
- Permanent residence applicants in Canada who
- used Express Entry to submit their permanent residence application, and
- have received an acknowledgment of receipt letter (A75)
- Open work permit pilot program for permanent residence applicants in the spouse or common-law partner in Canada class (A70)
- Foreign physicians coming to work in Quebec (C10)
- Refugee claimants (S61)
- Failed refugee claimants waiting for removal who need to support themselves (S62)
- Persons under an unenforceable removal order (S62)
- Live-in caregivers who have submitted their permanent residence application (A71)
- In-Canada applicants under the Home Child-Care Provider Pilot or the Home Support Worker Pilot (C90) and their family members (C91)
- Post-graduation work permit extension (C43)
- Destitute students (H81)
- Holders of a temporary resident permit that’s valid for a minimum of 6 months (H82)
- Start-up visa workers (A75)
- International Experience Canada: Extend your participation or change conditions on your work permit (C21)

## LMIA-required applicants
- Seafood-processing workers
- Agricultural workers who are not part of the Seasonal Agricultural Worker Program

## Visitors to Canada
- Visitors in Canada applying for an initial study permit, work permit or both who are accompanying a spouse holding a low-skilled work permit

title: If you lose your job
text:
## If you lose your job
If you lose the job connected to your employer-specific work permit, you must stop working for this or any other employer.
You need to leave Canada by the “ Must leave by ” date printed on your work permit if you
- can’t get a new job offer, or
- don’t apply for another immigration program

## If you have an open work permit and you lose your job
If you are an open work permit holder, your job isn’t connected to your work permit.
An open work permit lets you work for any employer in Canada, except those who
- are on the non-compliant list , or
- offer, on a regular basis, striptease, erotic dance, escort services or erotic massages

## If you want to stay in Canada and continue working
If you lose the job connected to your employer-specific work permit and want to continue working in Canada, you must
- get a new job offer and apply to change the conditions on your work permit
- stay in Canada
- stop working for this or any other employer until your new work permit is approved or we send you a work authorization email
If we approve your application to change the conditions on your work permit, we’ll issue you a new work permit.
Before you apply, you need some information and documents from your new employer. What you need will depend on whether the employer needs a labour market impact assessment to hire you .
If you apply to change the conditions of your work permit before your current work permit expires, you might be able to keep working with a work authorization .
Apply to change the conditions on your work permit

## If you want to stay in Canada as a visitor
If you want to extend your stay in Canada as a visitor, you need to apply for a visitor record .
You can’t work as a visitor unless you’re a worker authorized to work without a work permit .
Apply to extend your stay in Canada as a visitor

## If you want to stay in Canada as a student
If you want to study in Canada, you may need to apply for a study permit. Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study in Canada.
Some international students can work while they study in Canada .
Learn more about studying in Canada as an international student

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: Who can apply
text:
## Who can extend

## Who can apply
This application is for you if you
- want to extend your work permit
- need to make changes to the conditions on your work permit, such as
- the type of work you can do
- the employer you can work for
- where you can work
- This includes restrictions because you needed a medical exam . For instance, you received an open work permit with restrictions on working in health care because you hadn’t completed a medical exam.
- You can remove the conditions on where you can work once you get a medical exam.
- need to change your gender on your work permit
- If you identify as a different gender than the one on your work permit, use this application and include the Request for a Change of Sex or Gender Identifier form [IRM 0002] (PDF, 1.47 MB) .
- If we made a mistake on your work permit, you can ask to amend a valid temporary resident document .
If you don’t have a work permit but want to work in Canada temporarily, find out what you need to do .

## Employer-specific work permits
You need to apply to extend or change the conditions of your work permit if:
- your job is extended
- there are changes to your current job, such as:
- a change in your pay
- new responsibilities
- you’re offered a different job
- you want to work for a new employer
You can’t start working at a different job or for a new employer until you get your work permit with the new conditions.

## Work permits for Quebec skilled workers who applied for the Programme de sélection des travailleurs qualifiés New
You may be eligible for an employer-specific work permit to keep working in Quebec for up to 12 months if you
- submitted a demande de sélection permanente to Quebec for an application under the Programme de sélection des travailleurs qualifiés
- currently hold, or recently held an employer-specific work permit under the International Mobility Program (IMP) or the Temporary Foreign Workers Program (TFWP) for a job in Quebec
- will work for the same employer in Quebec
Find out more about this work permit .

## Open work permits
If you have an open work permit, you may be able to extend it as long as you’re still eligible to work in Canada with an open work permit .

## Who can apply for an open work permit?
You may be eligible for an open work permit if you:
- are an international student who graduated from a designated learning institution and are eligible for the Post-Graduation Work Permit Program
- are a student who’s no longer able to meet the costs of your studies (destitute student)
- have an employer-specific work permit and are being abused or at risk of being abused in relation to your job in Canada
- applied for permanent residence in Canada
- are a dependent family member of someone who applied for permanent residence
- are the spouse or common-law partner of a skilled worker or international student
- are the spouse or common-law partner of an applicant of the Atlantic Immigration Pilot Program
- are a refugee, refugee claimant, protected person or their family member
- are under an unenforceable removal order
- are a temporary resident permit holder
- are a young worker participating in special programs

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: What to do if your work permit expires or is expiring
text:
## What to do if your work permit expired

## If you apply before your work permit expires
If you apply to renew or change the conditions of your work permit before it expires, you can legally stay in Canada until a decision is made on your application.
If you need to travel outside Canada, make sure you understand how leaving Canada could affect your ability to work when you return .

## If you applied to extend your work permit
If you applied to extend your work permit and your initial permit expires while we’re processing your application, you have
- maintained your status
- authorization to work without a permit until we make a decision on your application, as long as you stay in Canada
You must keep working under the same conditions of your current work permit. If you have an employer-specific work permit, this means having the same
- employer
- job
- work location
If you’re an open work permit holder, you can usually change employers, jobs or locations, unless you have specific conditions listed on your work permit.

## Renewing provincial or territorial documents
Usually, while you’re on maintained status , you won’t be able to renew documents issued by your province or territory, such as your
- driver’s licence
- health card
Make sure your documents are valid before your work permit expires.

## Applying for a social insurance number (SIN) or updating the expiry of your SIN
Your SIN expires on the same date your work permit expires. You can continue working with an expired SIN until we make a decision on your work permit application.
You can apply for or update your SIN only once you receive your new work permit.
Find out what you need and how to apply for or renew your SIN .

## Proof you can continue to work
You can show your employer or others proof that you can keep working while we process your application. The type of proof depends on how you applied
- online
- on paper

## If you applied for another work permit
If you applied to change either your employer or job on your employer-specific work permit, and then your permit expires, you have
- maintained your status
- authorization to work without a permit until we make a decision, as long as you stay in Canada
- You must keep working for the employer named on your original work permit until we make a decision on your application.
You can’t start working with a new employer or in a new job
- until we approve your application, or
- unless you request and receive an authorization to work while we process your application

## Renewing provincial or territorial documents
Usually, while you’re on maintained status , you won’t be able to renew documents issued by your province or territory, such as your
- driver’s licence
- health card
Make sure your documents are valid before your work permit expires.

## Applying for a social insurance number (SIN) or updating the expiry of your SIN
You can continue working with an expired SIN until we make a decision on your work permit application.
You can apply for or update your SIN only once you receive your new work permit.
Find out what you need and how to apply for or renew your SIN .

## Proof you can continue to work
You can show your employer or others proof that you can keep working while we process your application. The type of proof depends on how you applied
- online
- on paper

## If you applied for a study permit
You can keep working only until your work permit expires . You cannot continue to work while waiting for a decision on your study permit application.
Also, you can’t start your studies until we make a decision on your study permit application, unless you’re authorized to study without a study permit .

## If you applied to extend your stay in Canada as a visitor (visitor record)
You can keep working only until your work permit expires . You cannot continue to work while waiting for a decision on your visitor application.

## Temporary resident permit applicants do not benefit from maintained status
Temporary resident permit (TRP) applicants can’t maintain temporary resident status while their application is being processed . This applies to both
- initial TRP applications, and
- any other TRP applications

title: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: Traveling outside Canada and re-entering
text:
## If you want to travel outside Canada
If you applied to renew your work permit before it expired, you can leave Canada and come back, but there are some things you need to know.

## On this page
- If you need to travel urgently
- Working when you return to Canada
- Documents you need to re-enter Canada

## If you need to travel urgently
If you need to travel urgently and your work permit is still being processed, you can request urgent processing .

## Working when you return to Canada
Whether you can work when you return depends on if your work permit renewal application was approved while you were away.

## If your work permit renewal application was approved
If your work permit renewal application was approved while you were away, you may be allowed to re-enter Canada as a worker .
You can work as soon as you enter Canada.

## If your work permit renewal application is still being processed
If your application is still being processed, you may be allowed to re-enter Canada as a visitor.
You can’t work until your work permit renewal has been approved.

## If you’re eligible to apply for a new work permit at a port of entry
If your application is still being processed and you meet the requirements, you may apply for a work permit upon entry .

## Documents you need to re-enter Canada
A work permit isn’t a travel document. It doesn’t give you authorization to travel to or re-enter Canada. Depending on your citizenship and nationality and how you plan to travel, you may need either
- a temporary resident visa (TRV), or
- an electronic travel authorization (eTA) , if required
Having an eTA or a visa doesn’t guarantee that you can re-enter Canada. You must show the border services officer that you meet all the requirements before you can re-enter.
Find out what other documents you’ll need to re-enter Canada.

title: How to request faster processing of your work permit extension if you need to travel urgently
text:
## How to request faster processing of your work permit extension if you need to travel urgently
If we’re still processing your work permit extension application, and you need to travel outside Canada urgently, you may be able to request urgent processing so you can continue to work in Canada when you return.
If you submit an incomplete request (for example, you’re missing documents), your application won’t be processed urgently.

## On this page
- Who can request urgent processing
- Prepare your documents
- How to request urgent processing
- After you request urgent processing

## Who can request urgent processing
You can request urgent processing if you meet all the criteria listed below:
- You applied for a work permit from within Canada before your initial work permit expired.
- You’re currently authorized to work in Canada without a work permit while we process your application.
- You must be travelling for 1 of these reasons :
- business travel that cannot be delayed
- a death in the family
- a serious illness in the family

## Prepare your documents
Prepare clear scans of all required documents listed below. If you don’t provide all the required documents, your request won’t be processed urgently.
All documents must be in either English or French. If they’re in another language, you must provide a certified translation .

## Required documents
- Proof of urgency (1 or more of the following)
- letter from your employer explaining why the travel is urgent and the impact on jobs or the success of the business
- death certificate
- evidence of serious illness (for example, a doctor’s note)
- Proof of travel due to the emergency
- copy of your plane, bus, train or boat ticket, OR
- proof of payment and the itinerary (if you don’t have your ticket yet)

## How to request urgent processing
Request urgent processing using our IRCC web form .
- Select, Update your application (for example, submit documents) .
- Select, Add a document to your application .
- In the “Tell us about your request” section:
- When asked, Did we ask you to add the document(s) to your application? , select, No, I want to add the document(s) to support or complete my application .
- In the textbox, copy and paste the text below and complete the details for your specific situation: Urgent work permit application in Canada – [Travel] or [Death/Serious illness in the family]
- Briefly explain why you need urgent processing.
- Include your travel date.
- State whether or not you can wait 10 business days.
- Keep your explanations brief and factual. Ensure names and dates match your documents .
- Upload your documents.
- Under “Upload your document(s)”, attach the documents you prepared .
Submit an IRCC web form

## If you need to make changes to your request
Use the IRCC web form to update your submitted request. If your situation has changed (for example, if your travel date changes), submit a web form with new supporting documents.
Unless your situation changes, you shouldn’t submit multiple web forms for the same request, or there may be delays.

## After you request urgent processing
We aim to mail the document to you before your travel date. If that isn’t possible, we aim to have the approval in our system, so border services officers can see it before your return date.
Urgent processing is not guaranteed.

text:
## Hire a home care worker (caregiver)
There are a few ways you can hire a home care worker (caregiver). Your options depend on
- whether you’re inside or outside Quebec
- where the home care worker (caregiver) will work
The information on this page applies to employers looking to hire a
- home child care provider ( National Occupation Classification 44100 )
- home support worker ( National Occupation Classification 44101 )
If you need to hire a worker in another occupation , follow the process to hire a foreign worker .

## On this page
- Hire a worker who’s in Canada
- Hire a worker who’s outside Canada
- Hire a worker as an employer in Quebec

## Hire a worker who’s in Canada
If you’re an employer (outside Quebec), you can hire a home care worker through one of the programs below.

## Home Care Worker Immigration Pilots: Workers in Canada stream : Option 1 of 4
Closed
The Home Care Worker Immigration pilots : Workers in Canada stream allows Canadian employers (outside Quebec) to hire qualified home care workers already in Canada.
How to hire under this pilot

## Home Child Care Provider and Home Support Worker pilots : Option 2 of 4
Closed to new applicants on June 17, 2024
You can only hire workers through these pilots if either
- the worker already has an open work permit without restrictions that would prevent them from working in child care or health services
- the worker already has a work permit under one of the pilots

## Temporary Foreign Worker Program : Option 3 of 4
You can only hire workers through this program if they meet these 2 conditions:
- the worker either
- already has a work or study permit
- is allowed to work in Canada without a work permit (this doesn’t apply to business visitors )
- will work in Quebec
- you can get a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) and have your candidate apply for a new LMIA-based work permit
Hire through the Temporary Foreign Worker

## International Mobility Program (open work permits other than the pilots) : Option 4 of 4
You can only hire workers under this program if
- the worker already has an open work permit without restrictions that would prevent them from working in child care or health services

## Hire a worker who’s outside Canada
If you’re an employer (outside Quebec), you can hire a home care worker through one of the programs below.

## Home Care Worker Immigration Pilots: Applicants not working in Canada stream : Option 1 of 4
Closed
How to hire under this pilot (once it opens)

## Home Child Care Provider and Home Support Worker pilots : Option 2 of 4
Closed to new applicants on June 17, 2024
You can only hire workers through these pilots if either
- you already submitted a job offer to a worker, and they submitted their permanent residence application before the program closed
- the worker already has an open work permit without restrictions that would prevent them from working in child care or health services

## Temporary Foreign Worker Program : Option 3 of 4
You can only hire through this program if the worker will work in Quebec.
Hire through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program .

## Hire a worker as an employer in Quebec
If you’re an employer in Quebec, you can hire a home care worker who’s outside or in Canada through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program .

title: Hire a provincial nominee
text:
## Hire a provincial nominee
The Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) lets provinces and territories nominate immigrants who meet local labour market needs and other priorities for permanent residence.
Each province and territory designs its own PNP streams, including those that aim to recruit and retain
- skilled and semi-skilled workers
- entrepreneurs and investors
- post-secondary graduates
Candidates must show that they can support themselves economically and plan to live in the nominating province or territory. IRCC and the nominating province or territory work together to ensure candidates are eligible for the program. In addition:
- we assess whether candidates are admissible to Canada
- provinces and territories set other program requirements, such as registration, that employers must follow
- employers must make a qualifying job offer to eligible candidates

## Explore the provincial and territorial programs
Provinces and territories use the Express Entry system, a non-Express Entry system or both to operate their PNP.
Select a province or territory to learn about their PNP programs
- Alberta
- British Columbia
- Manitoba
- New Brunswick
- Newfoundland and Labrador
- Northwest Territories
- Nova Scotia
- Nunavut
- Ontario
- Prince Edward Island
- Quebec
- Saskatchewan
- Yukon
Nunavut does not have a provincial nominee program. Learn more about how to immigrate to Nunavut .
Quebec does not have a provincial nominee program. Learn more about Quebec’s immigration programs

## Choose an application process

## Hiring using Express Entry
Processing time: We couldn’t load the data. Try again
Provinces and territories use the federal Express Entry process in 2 ways: to invite candidates from their PNP to apply to the Express Entry pool, or to search the pool for candidates who meet their hiring needs.
Candidate requirements
- Meet the minimum criteria of at least 1 of the 3 federal immigration programs managed through Express Entry
- Meet the requirements of the province or territory’s Express Entry PNP stream
- Have an active Express Entry profile
- They can create it on their own or follow the instructions provided by the province or territory.
Once a candidate meets these requirements, the province or territory will contact them to continue with the nomination process, which might involve additional steps for you, the employer.

## Finding a qualified candidate
Check with the province or territory where you’re hiring to identify candidates through their Express Entry portal who meet your workforce needs.

## Supporting a known candidate

title: Extend a temporary worker’s permit
text:
## Extend a temporary worker’s permit
Work permit extension for workers in Quebec
Starting March 13, 2026, your worker may be eligible for a labour market impact assessment (LMIA) exemption.
Find out more about this exemption .
The temporary worker must apply to extend or change the conditions of their work permit if you want to
- extend their employment beyond the expiry date of the work permit
- substantially change their occupation, wages or conditions
- hire them after they’ve worked in Canada for a different employer

## Before the worker applies to extend or change their permit
What you (the employer) must do depends on whether you need a labour market impact assessment (LMIA).
Find out if you need an LMIA .

## If you need an LMIA
You must do the following:
- Apply for a new LMIA as soon as possible so your worker gets the LMIA on time.
- If you’re in Quebec, you may also need a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (Certificat d’acceptation du Québec) (CAQ).
- Give your worker
- a valid job offer
- proof that you applied for the LMIA or CAQ
Check LMIA application processing times .

## The worker should not apply for an extension while waiting for the LMIA
They can only apply for a work permit extension without an LMIA if their current permit expires in less than 2 weeks.
If they apply for their work permit extension at the same time that you (the employer) apply for the LMIA, they must submit the LMIA within 90 days , or their application may be refused.

## If you don’t need an LMIA
You need to
- submit a new offer of employment , and
- pay the employer compliance fee

## When you don’t need to pay the fee or submit an offer of employment
You don’t need to submit an offer of employment if
- the worker you hire has an open work permit , or
- you’re exempt from the employer compliance process
You may not need to pay the employer compliance fee if the worker is exempt from paying the work permit processing fee.
See employer compliance exemptions for more details.

## What the temporary worker needs to do

## If the conditions of their work permit are changing
The temporary worker should apply to change the conditions of their work permit as soon as possible if
- their occupation, wages or conditions (such as work location) at work are changing substantially
- they’re changing employers
They should apply at least 30 days before the expiry date of their original work permit.
They’ll still maintain their status and be authorized to work without a permit under the conditions of their original work permit. However, they may not start the new work until a new work permit is issued.

## If a worker in Canada wants to change employers
A worker already in Canada with an employer-specific work permit may be able to start working for you right away if you
- have a valid labour market impact assessment (LMIA), or
- can hire in an LMIA-exempt situation using the Employer Portal
Find out more about workers in Canada who want to change employers .

## If they want to extend their work permit
If your worker applies to extend their work permit before it expires and the conditions of their original work permit are staying the same,
- they maintain their status in Canada while we process their application
and
- they’re authorized to keep working under the conditions of the original work permit until a decision is made
- If they have an employer-specific work permit, this means that they must continue in the same job, employer and work location.
If you need proof that the worker is authorized to continue working while we process their application, they can give you one of the following:
- A letter (WP-EXT except PGWP) from their online account that proves they’re allowed to work until a specific date or until we process their application, whichever comes first.
- Even if we don’t process the worker’s application by the date on their letter, they can legally keep working until we make a decision.
- If you need proof that the worker can work past the specified date, they can contact us .
- Proof that they submitted their application if they applied on paper.
- The request letter from us asking for more documents to process their work permit application.

## If the worker has an open work permit
Temporary workers with an open work permit don’t need to extend their permit to begin working for a new employer. They only need to extend their work permit if it’s about to expire.
Find out more about what the temporary worker has to do to apply to extend their existing work permit .

title: Extend a worker’s permit: Workers in Quebec
text:
Extend a worker’s permit

## Workers in Quebec
If you’re a Quebec employer, you may not need a new labour market impact assessment (LMIA) to extend your worker’s permit.
This means that you need to submit only an offer of employment to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).
If the worker can extend their work permit, they can continue to work for you for up to 12 months.
Follow these steps:
- Make sure your job offer is eligible

## Make sure your job offer is eligible
The job offer is eligible if the work is in Quebec. It doesn’t matter if you previously hired the worker with or without an LMIA.
- Make sure your worker is eligible

## Make sure your worker is eligible
There are certain requirements that your worker must meet, such as the following:
- The worker applied for a demande de sélection permanente , which means that
- the Quebec government invited them to apply for permanent residence through the Programme de sélection des travailleurs qualifiés (skilled worker selection program)
- they accepted the invitation
- The worker is already working for you.
- The worker’s employer-specific work permit is in 1 of these situations:
- It will expire on or before December 31, 2026.
- It expired, but the worker
- already applied to extend it before the expiry date
- maintains their status
- It expired between March 13, 2026 and December 31, 2026, but the worker is out of status (because they didn’t extend their permit).
The worker doesn’t have to work the same job as the one they worked under the expiring permit.
Find out more about the worker’s eligibility .
- Submit the offer of employment

## Submit the offer of employment
If your worker and the job offer are eligible, you must do the following:
- Submit an offer of employment to us in the Employer Portal and follow these steps:
- Don’t pay the employer compliance fee ($230).
- Select “No, I am exempt from paying fees for this Offer of Employment” in the Employer Portal.
- Upload a letter explaining that you don’t have to pay the fee under this exemption for Quebec employers.
- Use LMIA exemption code R01 when you fill out the online form.
- Type the code PPTR2PRQC2026 in the Job Title field (for priority processing).
- Give the worker the offer of employment number. The number
- starts with the letter “A” followed by 7 digits
- is given to you after you submit the offer of employment in the Employer Portal
After you complete these steps, the worker
- can apply for their work permit extension
- must apply on or before December 31, 2026

title: Who needs a labour market impact assessment
text:
Hire a temporary foreign worker

## Find out if you need a labour market impact assessment
A labour market impact assessment (LMIA) determines if the hiring of a temporary foreign worker will have a positive or negative effect on Canada’s labour market.
A positive LMIA confirms that
- no Canadians or permanent residents are available to do the job
- there is a need for a temporary foreign worker
Most employers need an LMIA before they can hire a temporary foreign worker.

## If the worker already has an open work permit
You do not need an LMIA if the worker has an open work permit .

## On this page
- Determine if you need an LMIA
- How to hire if you need an LMIA
- How to hire if you don’t need an LMIA
- Hiring in Quebec
- Hiring top talent with faster processing

## Determine if you need an LMIA
Before you hire the worker, you must determine if
- you need an LMIA
- the worker needs a work permit
Follow these steps:
- Review the
- LMIA exemption codes to determine if you need an LMIA
- work permit exemptions to determine if the worker needs a work permit
- Select the LMIA exemption code or work permit exemption that seems most relevant to your situation.
- Read the detailed descriptions to determine if the exemption applies to you.

## If an exemption applies to your situation
If an LMIA exemption applies
- you can hire without an LMIA
- the worker needs a work permit
- you must include the LMIA exemption code in your offer of employment
If a work permit exemption applies
- the worker doesn’t need a work permit, but
- they must check if they need a visa to come to Canada

## If an exemption does not apply to your situation
If an exemption doesn’t apply, then
- you need an LMIA to hire the worker and
- the worker needs a work permit

## How to hire if you need an LMIA
If you determine that you need an LMIA, you’ll need to hire through the Temporary Foreign Worker Program.
Employment and Social Development Canada
- manages the program
- processes LMIA applications
- issues the decision letter
If you receive a positive LMIA decision letter, you need to take both of these steps:
- Provide each worker with
- a copy of the decision letter
- the letter’s Annex A – Employment details
- Tell them to apply for a work permit .
Learn more about hiring with an LMIA.

## How to hire if you don’t need an LMIA
You can hire without an LMIA through the International Mobility Program.
Learn more about hiring without an LMIA.

## Hiring in Quebec
You’ll need to meet different requirements depending on whether you’re hiring with or without an LMIA.

## If you’re hiring with an LMIA
You need to
- get a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) from the Ministère de l’Immigration, de la Francisation et de l’Intégration (MIFI)
- give a copy of the CAQ to your worker
When the worker applies for a work permit, they must submit
- a copy of the CAQ
- a copy of the positive LMIA decision letter
Find out how to hire with an LMIA in Quebec.

## If you’re hiring without an LMIA
The worker doesn’t need a CAQ if you’re hiring through the International Mobility Program.
Learn more about hiring without an LMIA.

## Hiring top talent with faster processing
The Global Skills Strategy (GSS) allows you to hire highly skilled workers and get the application processed faster.
Depending on the job, you can hire through the GSS with or without an LMIA .
Find out how to hire through the GSS.

title: Employer compliance exemptions
text:
## Employer compliance exemptions

## Examples of this type of organization
These are examples of organizations recognized under Foreign Missions and International Organizations Act :
- International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)
- Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
- United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
- Office of the European Union in Montréal
See the complete list .

## Examples of work that falls under this category
Examples of this category of work:
- United States (U.S.) Internal Revenue Service (IRS) employees coming to Canada temporarily to perform audits and conduct criminal investigations
- U.S. employees of the Peace Bridge Authority working in toll booths on the Canadian side of the border
- interns working at diplomatic missions or international organizations in Canada
Some employers don’t need to use the Employer Portal or are exempt from the employer compliance fee.

## Employers that don’t need to use the Employer Portal
- international missions or consular posts
- an international organization recognized under the Foreign Missions and International Organizations Act
- examples of this type of organization
- a foreign government
- an owner or operator of an international bridge or tunnel
Examples of work that falls under the categories outlined above .

## Employer compliance fee exemptions
If you’re part of any of the programs, agreements or labour market impact assessment (LMIA) exemption categories listed below, the temporary worker is fee exempt and you don’t need to pay the employer compliance fee when you hire them.
In the Employer Portal , when asked if you’re paying fees, select “No, I am exempt from paying fees for this Offer of Employment.”
You need to give proof that you’re part of these programs or agreements when you submit an offer of employment . Proof can be a letter explaining how you’re part of the program, agreement or LMIA exemption category. Upload the letter of explanation in the Proof of fee exemption field when you submit your offer.

## Programs, public policies and agreements exempt from the employer compliance fee

## Work permit extension for workers in Quebec
Starting March 13, 2026, your worker may be eligible for a labour market impact assessment exemption if they
- will work in Quebec
- meet certain requirements, such as
- they’re extending their employer-specific work permit
- they’re already working for you
- they applied for a Demande de sélection permanente (permanent selection application) under the Programme de sélection des travailleurs qualifiés (skilled worker selection program)
If your worker is eligible for this public policy, you do not have to pay the employer compliance fee.
Find out more about this exemption .

## Non-trade international agreements
These programs or agreements fall under the LMIA exemption category R204(a) and include
- Fulbright Program (Canada-U.S.) —worker is fee-exempt as per R299(h)
- Roosevelt Campobello International Park —worker is fee-exempt as per R299(h)
- U.S. government personnel (must be working in Canada on official U.S. government business)—worker is fee-exempt as per R299(g) or (k)

## Reciprocal employment
These programs or agreements fall under the LMIA exemption category R205(b) and include
- cultural agreements —worker is fee-exempt as per R299(h)
- Canada-China cultural exchange—worker is fee-exempt as per R299(h)

## Work related to a research program
These programs or agreements fall under the LMIA exemption category R205(c)(i) and include workers who are fee-exempt as per R299(e) :
- scientists or post-doctoral fellows sponsored by Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd.
- scientists or scholars sponsored by:
- National Research Council of Canada
- National Resources Canada and its associated departments
- Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
- research chair positions:
- Canada Research Chair
- Canada Excellence Research Chair
- similar research chair positions

## Unremunerated charitable or religious work
These programs or agreements fall under the LMIA exemption category R205(d) and include workers who do not receive remuneration :
- Temporary workers who are exempt from the work permit processing fee as per R299(f) .
- The temporary worker cannot receive payment for their work. They may receive a living expense stipend, which should be below the prevailing minimum wage. Otherwise, they should receive only non-monetary benefits (for example, housing and health care).
The proof of fee exemption document that you provide when you submit an offer of employment should detail how the worker is or is not remunerated for this exemption to apply. Simply indicating that the employer is a charitable or religious organization is not sufficient.

title: Hire through the Global Skills Strategy: How to get faster processing
text:
## How to get faster processing
- Give the temporary foreign worker the documents and information they need to apply

## Give the temporary foreign worker the documents and information they need to apply
You must give the temporary foreign worker the documents and information they need to submit their work permit application.

## If you need a labour market impact assessment (LMIA)
You’ll need to give the worker
- an employment contract
- a job offer letter
- the LMIA decision letter showing that you have a positive LMIA through the Global Talent Stream of the Temporary Foreign Worker Program
Find out how to apply for an LMIA .

## If you don’t need an LMIA
You’ll need to give the worker
- an offer of employment number
- the LMIA exemption code
- proof that you paid the employer compliance fee
Find out how to submit an offer of employment .
- The worker applies for a work permit Family members of the worker

## The worker applies for a work permit
The worker must
- apply for a work permit online from outside Canada
- pay the processing fees
- submit the results of their biometric exam within 2 weeks of submitting the application (if needed)
- get a medical exam
- make sure the application is complete (including all the documents listed in their visa office instructions)
Incomplete applications are not eligible for the GSS and take longer to process.
If the worker is not eligible for the GSS, you can check our processing times for non-GSS work permits .
The worker doesn’t need to apply separately for a visa or electronic travel authorization (eTA). We issue the documents they need when we process their work permit application.
Learn about the work permit application process and the required documents .

## Family members of the worker
The worker’s family members (spouse or common-law partner and dependent children) only qualify for 2-week processing if they
- apply at the same time as the worker
- submit a complete application
